Mia Chen: Heads-up — on an 8xA100 LL128 job we saw periodic allreduce stalls of ~2-3s right after a proto selection transition. KV-cache warmup spikes at the same timestamps. Uploaded trace and logs. :thinking:
perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/1999991111/run-8xA100.trace (:eyes:)
Ryan O'Neill: Can you paste the nvprof / timeline snippet? wonder if kernel selector flips to a fallback kernel during proto phase causing syncs
Mia Chen: Paste of the relevant slice:
```
[timeline] 00:10:23.120 forward_step start
[comm] LL128 allreduce success (20ms)
[kernel_selector] choose_path -> proto_path (reason: small_batch+long_seq)
[comm] allreduce wait 2400ms
[kvcache] miss rate jump 0.02 -> 0.45
[kernel] selected fallback_matmul_cuda_slow
```
rkprof --flame run-1999991111.trace | head
```
Sasha Patel: small_batch+long_seq -> proto makes sense. batching heuristic might be shrinking microbatch size at that phase. if batch < X -> prefer proto algo (tree/ring) which is terrible on 8 GPUs with our channel map
Devon Liu: Interesting. I ran a quick sweep locally: forcing algo=ring made latency worse, algo=tree improved some cases but throughput dropped. When I forced ll128=off (fall back to LL), stalls disappeared but CPU-side kernel times increased slightly.
Mia Chen: I also tried pinning channels=8 and ll128=on. stalls reduced (median p95 down ~700ms) but variance still high. KV warmup correlation is strong — when microbatches are sparse, kv cache misses cascade and trigger extra kernels that seem to serialize comms.
Ryan O'Neill: Two quick experiments to try: 1) prewarm KV across TP shards at startup (e.g., N warm requests) 2) force kernel selection logging to DEBUG and collect selector decision stream. Can you add the selector log dump?
Mia Chen: Will do. selector logs look like:
```
[selector] step=1023 model_block=37 chosen=quant_fast_v2 fallback=matmul_cuda_slow reason="proto_path" score_delta=0.12
[selector] step=1024 chosen=quant_fast_v2 reason="ll128_ok"
[selector] step=1025 chosen=quant_fast_v2 fallback=matmul_cuda_slow reason="kv_miss"
```
Sasha Patel: That kv_miss line is suspicious — selector reasoning ties proto choice to kv misses. Could be a heuristic bug where cost estimator undervalues LL128 when cache miss rate > threshold.
Devon Liu: I'll schedule a canary with two variants: A) force proto-path to always pick proto algo (control) B) disable proto preference (force LL path). We'll compare perf and tail-latency. I'll include channel-mapping const config.
Mia Chen: Also adding a small prewarm patch to runtime: send N=8 prefix requests across TP replicas to populate KV for typical seq lengths. Quick test on dev reduced p95 by ~300ms.
Ryan O'Neill: Nice. If prewarm helps, maybe we add it as an opt-in heuristic for low-load startups. But we still need to fix selector's scoring function.
Sasha Patel: Agreed. Also check kernel selector's quantized kernel profiles: there are cases where quant_fast_v2 regresses depending on sequence length — fallback triggers cause sync points. We should collect per-kernel occupancy and SM utilization at step boundaries.
Mia Chen: Filed IR-4572 with traces and selector logs, attached the canary plan, and noting steps to reproduce. cc @SRE.
infra-bot: Incident created: IR-4572 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/IR-4572) — assigned to eng-runtime.
Devon Liu: Will run the A/B canary tomorrow morning (UTC) and pipe perf traces to the ticket. :+1:
Ryan O'Neill: If you want, I can prototype a scoring delta fix: penalize proto_path when kv_miss_rate > 0.2 or when channel_util < 0.6.
Mia Chen: That sounds good. Thanks everyone — will update ticket with the prewarm PR and traces. :raised_hands:
